summary: Add a modern VLM-embedder baseline (GME-Qwen2VL-2B) and a training-free local-LLM reranker to the comparison table

results.name: gme_baseline
results.model_used: Alibaba-NLP/gme-Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct (2B, Qwen2-VL backbone, fp16). Encoder path: vendored GmeQwen2VL custom class (get_text_embeddings / get_image_embeddings), last-token L2-normalized pooling. Patched the vendored gme_inference.py for transformers 4.57 (old self.base.model.embed_tokens path broke because Qwen2VLModel now nests .language_model; delegated to self.base.model(input_ids, pixel_values, image_grid_thw) which does vision splice + mrope natively, then GME last-token pooling unchanged). Smoke-tested OK.
results.gpu_used: GPU 1 (A6000). GPU 0 was free at start but a non-killable orphan CUDA context (PID in another namespace, 41GB) appeared after my first run, so per GPU policy I moved to free GPU 1 (<500MiB) for the actual encode.
results.paired_vs_current_best: GME LOSES on every framing. Human-30 vs lora384_bm25_pub (0.756): GME-dense dMRR=-0.290 sign_p=0.007 W4/L17; GME+BM25 dMRR=-0.304 sign_p=0.004 W3/L16. Synth-1706 vs recomputed LoRA+BM25 (0.903): GME-dense dMRR=-0.473 sign_p<1e-4 W74/L1075; GME+BM25 dMRR=-0.123 sign_p<1e-4 W119/L361. (Also computed R@1 and R@10 framings — all favor the current best; R@10 human-30 GME+BM25 is the only non-significant one, p=0.18.)
results.multipos_human30: n/a — cached multipos positives (data/novel_cache/multipos_judge.json) were built from a SigLIP/LoRA top-15 candidate pool; GME's top items can fall outside it, so reusing them would undercount GME's valid hits unfairly. A fair version needs pool expansion with GME top-15 + EXAONE re-judging of new candidates (out of scope). Documented in JSON multipos_note.
results.disk_added: ~8.8GB HF model cache (the GME safetensors ship as fp32, ~8.8GB on disk, cast to fp16 at load) + ~20MB of gme__*.npy embedding caches. Cleaned interrupted .incomplete blobs. ~48GB free remaining.
results.notes: Confirms the task's prediction: a much bigger contemporary 2B VLM embedder does NOT match the cheap SigLIP2+text-LoRA+BM25 pipeline on this narrow Korean fashion catalogue. GME's image-only dense retrieval is genuinely weak here (human-30 dense 0.467 even below the zero-shot SigLIP baseline 0.571; diagnostics confirmed embeddings are correct and aligned — 11/30 GT at rank 1, median rank 3, not a bug). On synth, GME+BM25 (0.780) is carried almost entirely by the lexical channel — the BM25 weight selected on val hit the grid edge (w=0.5), and an extended grid (w up to 2.0) pushes synth to ~0.852 but drops human-30 to 0.376 (i.e. approaching pure BM25, overfitting the tiny val set). I deliberately kept the SAME small-weight BM25 grid [0.05..0.50] / n in {10,20,50} as run_final_suite.py so the fusion comparison is apples-to-apples with the existing pipeline. Files: src/novel/run_gme_baseline.py (encode/report; rerun cheap via cached npy), src/novel/gme_inference.py (vendored+patched encoder), output/novel/gme_baseline.json (full results incl. per-query ranks + paired tests for MRR/R@1/R@10). Embeddings cached at data/novel_cache/gme__{gallery_img,val_gallery_img,eval_q,val_q,synth_eval_q}.npy.

results.name: llm_reranker
results.model_used: LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.5-7.8B-Instruct via vLLM 0.6.4 (XFORMERS backend, temp 0, max_tokens 4), pointwise graded relevance 0-3 over top-k=10 candidates; 24,530 (query,candidate) judgements cached to data/novel_cache/reranker_judge.json
results.gpu_used: GPU 0 (was 4 MiB free; EXAONE used ~41 GB at gpu_mem_util=0.85; freed back to 4 MiB after run)
results.singlepos_human30: PURE LLM reorder (w=inf, no tuning, no leakage): R@1=0.600 R@5=0.833 R@10=0.900 MRR=0.6871 ci[0.539,0.826]. TUNED (w_llm=0.5, val-selected): R@1=0.700 R@5=0.833 R@10=0.900 MRR=0.7545 ci[0.613,0.886]. Base (current-best LoRA+BM25, n10/w0.15) = 0.756. => tie at best (tuned), pure variant HURTS single-pos because EXAONE promotes other valid-looking tops above the single labeled GT.
results.synth1706: PURE: R@1=0.760 R@5=0.836 R@10=0.846 MRR=0.7950 ci[0.777,0.813]. TUNED(w=0.5): R@1=0.791 R@5=0.843 R@10=0.846 MRR=0.8150 ci[0.797,0.832]. Base used here (same n10/w0.15 op point) synth MRR=0.8100. NOTE: this base is the human-eval-tuned operating point, weaker on synth than the synth-optimal dense+BM25 reference (0.903) — paired test is rerank-vs-same-base, valid, but absolute synth MRR is below the 0.903 reference by construction.
results.paired_vs_current_best: vs un-reranked LoRA+BM25 base (= published current best, MRR 0.756, ranks_match=1). SINGLE-POS human-30: pure dMRR=-0.0689 sign_p=0.508 W3/L6; tuned dMRR=-0.0015 sign_p=1.000 W3/L3 (tie). MULTI-POS human-30 (mean 5.07 pos/query, same multipos.json pool+judge): pure dMRR=+0.0556 sign_p=0.219 W5/L1; tuned dMRR=+0.0539 sign_p=0.219 W5/L1 (gain but N=30 underpowered, NS). SYNTH-1706 (high power): pure dMRR=-0.0149 sign_p=0.0061 W60/L95 (significantly WORSE); tuned dMRR=+0.0050 sign_p=0.0220 W58/L35 (significantly BETTER). So a light LLM blend helps at high power; aggressive pure reordering hurts.
results.multipos_human30: PURE: R@1=0.867 R@5=1.000 R@10=1.000 MRR=0.9111 ci[0.822,0.983]. TUNED(w=0.5): R@1=0.867 R@5=1.000 R@10=1.000 MRR=0.9094 ci[0.818,0.983]. Base multi-pos MRR=0.8556. Both variants gain ~+0.054 MRR but not significant at N=30 (sign_p=0.219, W5/L1). Multi-pos is the FAIR framing here: the reranker's habit of promoting other valid white/long-sleeve tops is rewarded, not penalized.
results.disk_added: ~0.5 MB (reranker_judge.json 462 KB + llm_reranker.json 5.4 KB). NO model download — EXAONE-3.5-7.8B was already cached (~30 GB on disk).
results.notes:
Implementation: src/novel/run_llm_reranker.py (output output/novel/llm_reranker.json, judge cache data/novel_cache/reranker_judge.json, log output/novel/llm_reranker_run.log). Base ranking = current-best LoRA384 dense + BM25 at the published op point n=10/w=0.15, which EXACTLY reproduces lib.load_refs()['lora384_bm25_pub'] (MRR 0.756, ranks_match=1) — chosen so the paired test is literally "LLM-rerank vs current best". Two variants: PURE (hard sort by LLM grade desc, base desc; zero HP, zero eval leakage) and TUNED (trust-weight w_llm in {0,0.5,1,2,4,8,inf} selected on VALIDATION only; selected w=0.5, a LIGHT blend). Reorder stays inside the SigLIP top-10 candidate set, so multipos.json positives apply unchanged (rebuilt the exact run_multipos.py pool=union top-15 over 6 methods + GT, labeled by cached multipos_judge.json; mean 5.07 pos/query). EXAONE grade distribution on eval top-10 = [0:40, 1:110, 2:125, 3:25].

HARD/AMBIGUOUS QUERY CHECK (the key diagnostic): 3/30 queries (all short_ambiguous: idx 0/12/17, base ranks 378/191/483) have their single GT OUTSIDE top-10 — the candidate-preserving reranker structurally CANNOT fix these; they are single-positive labeling artifacts. On short_ambiguous queries pure rerank HURTS single-pos MRR (0.701->0.495) because EXAONE correctly promotes OTHER valid white/long-sleeve tops above the one labeled GT; under multi-pos those promotions are credited (0.856->0.911). long_specific improves (base 0.933 -> tuned 1.000). 

VERDICT (matches the honest expectation in the task): gold N=30 single-pos is a tie; multi-pos gains but underpowered; the only statistically clean signal is synth-1706, where a LIGHT LLM blend (w=0.5) gives a small significant gain (+0.005 MRR, sign_p=0.022) while aggressive pure LLM reordering significantly hurts (-0.015, sign_p=0.006). Net: training-free LLM reranking is at best a marginal, weight-sensitive improvement on this small in-domain catalogue and does NOT beat the LoRA+BM25 current best on the locked human-30 single-positive metric. Caveat to flag in the writeup: the synth base here is the human-tuned op point (0.810), not the synth-optimal dense+BM25 (0.903), so synth absolute numbers are not directly comparable to that reference — only the paired rerank-vs-same-base deltas are.

verds.honest_verdict:
VERIFIED HONEST. The gme_baseline method is clean and its reported numbers reproduce exactly from the on-disk caches. GME genuinely loses to the current-best LoRA+BM25 on every framing; the report is candid about this and even about GME's weaknesses.

(1) NO EVAL LEAKAGE. The only HP is the BM25 fusion (n, w), and it is tuned exclusively on validation: _select_bm25(dense_val, val_bm25, vgt) uses only val_gt; the same val-selected (n0,w0) is then frozen and applied to both eval and synth. eval_gt (egt) appears only inside lib.ranks_of for final scoring, never in selection (confirmed by grep). The LoRA synth reference is tuned the same way (val-only, picked n=50/w=0.2). The BM25 grid [0.05..0.50]/n{10,20,50} is byte-identical to run_final_suite.py, so the fusion comparison is apples-to-apples — the agent did NOT widen the grid to favor GME (it explicitly notes an extended grid would help synth but kept the standard one; this is the conservative, anti-cherry-pick choice). Multi-pos was correctly declined: the cached multipos pool was built from SigLIP/LoRA top-15, so reusing it would undercount GME's hits; honestly marked n/a rather than reported unfairly.

(2) NUMBERS REPRODUCE. Independently recomputed from gme__*.npy + lib: human30 GME-dense MRR=0.4666, GME+BM25 MRR=0.4517; synth GME-dense 0.4299, GME+BM25 0.7798; val BM25 selection n=50/w=0.5/val_MRR=0.7626; synth LoRA+BM25 ref=0.9026 (matches published 0.903); refs baseline 0.5711 / lora384 0.6842 / lora_bm25_pub 0.756. Spot-checked paired tests: human30 GME-dense vs pub dMRR=-0.2895 sign_p=0.0072 W4/L17/T9 and synth GME+BM25 vs LoRA dMRR=-0.1227 W119/L361/T1226 — both match the JSON exactly.

(3) ENCODE ORDERING + FAIR COMPARISON. Gallery images encoded as (588,1536) over data.gallery_pids, and meta.gallery_pids == data.gallery_pids (True), so the scoring matrix Qe@Gi.T is aligned to gt. Embeddings are L2-normalized (mean norm 1.0). The comparison is GME+BM25 vs LoRA+BM25 (both fused), not GME+BM25 vs LoRA-dense — fair. No LLM reranker exists in this method (the task's reranker clause is boilerplate; gme_baseline is a dense embedder + BM25 fusion). GPU policy followed: encode log shows CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1.
verds.issues: No methodological issues. Minor/cosmetic only: (a) The vendored gme_inference.py was patched for transformers 4.57 (delegates to self.base.model with pixel_values/image_grid_thw for native vision splice + mrope, then GME last-token pooling). I did not re-run the encoder end-to-end to confirm the patch produces the model-card-equivalent embeddings — but the smoke-test behavior, correct 1536-dim L2-normalized output, and the sane retrieval quality (11/30 GT at rank 1 on human-30, dense MRR 0.467) indicate the encoder is functioning, not broken. (b) The val-selected BM25 weight w=0.5 sits at the grid edge; the agent flagged this and correctly chose NOT to extend the grid (extending would approach pure-BM25 and overfit the tiny val set). This is a defensible conservative call, and it works against GME on human-30, so it is not gaming. (c) synth GME+BM25 (0.780) is carried almost entirely by the lexical channel (dense alone only 0.430) — the agent states this plainly in notes. Verdict: a fair, well-documented losing baseline; nothing inflated.

verds.honest_verdict:
VERIFIED CLEAN. The llm_reranker method (training-free EXAONE-3.5-7.8B pointwise 0-3 grading, reorder within SigLIP top-10) holds up to adversarial scrutiny on all three requested axes. Files: src/novel/run_llm_reranker.py, output/novel/llm_reranker.json, data/novel_cache/reranker_judge.json.

(1) NO EVAL LEAKAGE. The only hyperparameter, the trust-weight w_llm, is selected purely on the validation split (rerank(base_val,...) over WLLM_GRID, argmax val MRR -> 0.5). I independently reproduced the val_w_table {0.0:0.8895, 0.5:0.9032, 1.0:0.8905, 2.0:0.8795, ...} and confirmed 0.5 is selected on val, not eval. The BM25 fusion weight is NOT tuned at all on eval: the base is fixed at the PUBLISHED operating point n=10/w=0.15, and ranks_of(base_eval) matches lib.load_refs()['lora384_bm25_pub'] elementwise (ranks_match=1, MRR 0.756 exact). Multipos positives are built by build_multipos_positives() which I confirmed is a line-for-line replica of run_multipos.py (same 6 methods, same rr=rerank_topn(S,bm25,50,0.2), same top-15 union + GT injection, same cached multipos_judge.json) — rebuilt mean positives = 5.07, matching the published multipos.json exactly.

(2) NUMBERS REPRODUCE. Recomputing from the cached judge (no LLM): base_eval MRR 0.75602; pure singlepos MRR 0.687091, multipos 0.911111, synth 0.795014; tuned singlepos 0.754498, multipos 0.909444, synth 0.814960 — all match llm_reranker.json to 6 dp, and the reported ranks vectors match. Spot-checked paired tests: pure synth dMRR=-0.014943 sign_p=0.006133 W60/L95 (significantly worse) and tuned synth dMRR=+0.005004 sign_p=0.022019 W58/L35 (significantly better) both reproduce exactly. Judge cache has 24530 keys (300 eval = 30x10, 7170 val, 17060 synth = 1706x10), grades in {0,1,2,3}, eval grade dist [40,110,125,25] as reported, and ZERO eval top-10 candidates are missing a judge key.

(3) CANDIDATE-SPACE / FAIRNESS. Confirmed the reranker never leaves the SigLIP candidate space: for pure AND tuned, on both eval and synth, the SET of items in the top-10 after rerank is identical to the base top-10 in every query (topk_set_changed=0); only the ORDER within the block changes. Non-top-10 tail scores are untouched (tail_score_changed=0), so no new candidate is injected and no positive outside top-10 can be reached. This is exactly what makes the multipos positives (drawn from a top-15 union pool) apply unchanged — positives inside the base top-10 average 2.8/query (the only ones rerank can reorder), the rest sit below and are unaffected. (GME-specific checks N/A; this is the LLM reranker.)

The verdict in the method report is honest and matches the evidence: pure (aggressive) reorder significantly HURTS high-power synth (sign_p=0.006) and hurts single-pos human-30 (artifact: it correctly promotes other valid white/long-sleeve tops above the single labeled GT); a light blend (tuned w=0.5) is a tie on single-pos human-30 and a small-but-significant WIN on synth (sign_p=0.022). The honest framing — single-pos penalizes the reranker's correct behavior, multi-pos is the fair view (+0.054 MRR, NS at N=30) — is well supported.
verds.issues:
No leakage or reproduction issues found. Minor, fully-disclosed caveats only:
- The reranker's BASE for paired tests is dense+BM25 at n=10/w=0.15 (multipos base MRR 0.8556), which is a DIFFERENT operating point than the published multipos.json dense_bm25 (n=50/w=0.2, MRR 0.8575) and the synth-optimal dense+BM25 reference (0.903). The report discloses this explicitly: the paired test is rerank-vs-SAME-base (valid), but the absolute synth MRR (0.795/0.815) sits below the 0.903 reference by construction because the base is the human-eval-tuned op point, not the synth-optimal one. This is a fair-comparison design choice (so the test is literally 'LLM-rerank vs current best'), not a flaw, and it is honestly stated.
- 3/30 single-pos eval queries have their GT outside the base top-10 (idx 0/12/17, ranks 378/191/483, confirmed). A candidate-preserving reranker structurally cannot fix these; this is correctly described as a single-positive labeling artifact, not hidden.
- The net practical gain is marginal and NOT significant at the human-30 N (multipos sign_p=0.219); only the high-power synth-1706 test reaches significance for the light blend (+0.005 MRR). Real but small effect — accurately characterized in the report, not overstated.

final.did_either_beat_current_best: No. Neither method beats the current-best LoRA+BM25 with statistical support on any framing. GME loses decisively on every framing (human-30 single, human-30 R@1/R@10, and synth-1706 for both dense and +BM25), all with sign_p well below 0.05 against the current best -- GME-dense even falls below the zero-shot SigLIP baseline (0.467 vs 0.571). The LLM reranker at best TIES the current best on the locked human-30 single-positive metric (tuned w=0.5: dMRR=-0.002, sign_p=1.00, W3/L3) -- it does not beat it. Where the LLM reranker shows positive deltas they are either underpowered or against a weaker base: (a) human-30 multipos +0.054 MRR is not significant at N=30 (sign_p=0.22, W5/L1); (b) the one statistically clean positive signal -- synth-1706 tuned +0.005 MRR, sign_p=0.022 -- is a paired delta against the SAME human-30-tuned base (synth 0.810), NOT against the synth-optimal LoRA+BM25 (0.903); its absolute synth MRR (0.815) sits ~0.09 BELOW the 0.903 reference. So it does not beat the current best on synth either. The aggressive pure-LLM variant actively HURTS synth (-0.015, sign_p=0.006). Net per our N=30 ceiling: GME = clear loss; LLM reranker = tie on the primary locked metric, with only a marginal, weight-sensitive, same-base improvement at high power. Both verifications confirmed leakage-free (HPs tuned on val only) and that all reported numbers reproduce exactly from on-disk caches.
final.recommendation:
For the thesis, report both as confirmatory negative/neutral results that reinforce the cheap-pipeline thesis -- do not promote either as a new best.

1) GME (2B VLM embedder): Frame exactly as predicted -- "a much larger contemporary 2B vision-language embedder (GME-Qwen2-VL-2B) does NOT beat our cheap SigLIP2 + text-only-LoRA + BM25 pipeline on this narrow Korean fashion catalogue." Quote: GME-dense human-30 MRR 0.467 (below even zero-shot SigLIP 0.571) and GME+BM25 0.452 vs current best 0.756 (sign_p=0.007 / 0.004); synth GME+BM25 0.780 vs 0.903 (sign_p<1e-28). State plainly that GME's synth 0.780 is carried almost entirely by the lexical (BM25) channel since dense alone is only 0.430. This is a strong "bigger model is not the answer here; domain-aligned text adaptation is" point. Note honestly that multipos was declined (the cached top-15 candidate pool was built from SigLIP/LoRA, so reusing it would unfairly undercount GME) -- this is a fairness virtue, not a gap to hide.

2) LLM reranker (EXAONE-3.5-7.8B, training-free pointwise 0-3 grading, reorder within SigLIP top-10): Present as an optional training-free add-on with a measured, modest, weight-sensitive effect -- NOT as a method that beats the baseline. Key honest framing: on the locked human-30 single-positive metric it is a statistical tie (0.754 vs 0.756). It cannot fix the 3/30 short-ambiguous queries whose single GT sits outside the SigLIP top-10 -- these are single-positive labeling artifacts. Use the multipos and synth results to explain WHY: the reranker correctly promotes other valid white/long-sleeve tops, which single-positive scoring penalizes but multi-positive scoring rewards (+0.054 MRR, though NS at N=30). The only clean win is synth tuned +0.005 (sign_p=0.022) against the same base, and you MUST caveat that this base is the human-tuned op point (0.810), not the synth-optimal 0.903 -- so it is a relative, not absolute, improvement. Also report that the aggressive pure variant HURTS synth (sign_p=0.006), motivating the LIGHT blend (w=0.5, val-selected). Bottom line for the writeup: "a light LLM rerank is at best a marginal add-on on this small in-domain catalogue and does not beat the LoRA+BM25 current best on our primary locked metric; the N=30 single-positive evaluation is the binding ceiling, and the multi-positive framing suggests part of the apparent ceiling is a labeling artifact rather than a model limitation." This honest negative framing is consistent with the project's defensibility-floor philosophy and avoids overclaiming.
